title: Turkey Sweet Potato Chili
seoTitle: Turkey Sweet Potato Chili | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Crock chili with diced sweet potato, black beans, and warm spices
subtitle: Crock chili with diced sweet potato, black beans, and warm spices
description: Ground turkey simmers with sweet potato cubes, black beans, fire-roasted tomatoes, and chili spices until thick and fragrant.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Turkey Sweet Potato Chili in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch turkey. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brown turkey and aromatics
steps.instruction: Brown turkey with onion and bell pepper in a skillet 10–12 minutes until turkey is crumbly and vegetables soften with lightly golden edges. Target 165°F at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Bloom spices
steps.instruction: Add garlic, chili powder, cumin, and paprika. Cook 2 minutes until spices smell toasted and coat the turkey evenly. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Transfer to crock
steps.instruction: Scrape mixture into slow cooker. Add sweet potato, beans, tomatoes, broth, and salt. Stir until combined and potatoes submerged. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Slow cook until tender
steps.instruction: Cook on low 5–6 hours until sweet potato pierces easily with a fork but still holds cube shape, not falling apart. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Turkey Sweet Potato Chili onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Adjust and serve
steps.instruction: Taste and adjust salt. Chili should be thick enough to mound on a spoon without running off immediately. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Do not stir aggressively—broken sweet potato thickens too much and turns paste-like.
Top with avocado and cilantro for fresh contrast to long-simmered flavors.
Swap half sweet potato for butternut squash in fall without changing cook time.
tonightSpread: Greek yogurt and hot sauce at the line.
leftovers: Chili baked over tater tots with cheese for a quick casserole.
Freeze portions for backup meals—reheat with extra broth.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Familiar chili night with a lighter twist. Sweet potato adds body and keeps the pot gluten-free and filling.
mealPrepNotes: Dice sweet potato uniform ½-inch so pieces cook evenly. Brown turkey before adding to crock. Station: Brown turkey in skillet first—raw turkey in crock makes greasy, bland chili. Station: Add sweet potato in last 2 hours on high if starting from cold crock. Station: Hold on warm with lid slightly vented so potatoes do not turn to mush.
